candidates.draft_body:
Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

'When that criminal saw that they were dead, he commanded that their FLESH BE BURNED WITH FIRE until they became ash, and that the wind scatter them. But the fire from morning till evening was kindled and did not touch them' — the CORPSES-RESIST-DESTRUCTION motif. Fire (4:1-2) → sea-and-millstones (4:3) → beasts-and-carrion-birds (4:4-5) → all fail to harm the martyrs' bodies. The motif parallels the THREE-YOUNG-MEN-IN-THE-FIERY-FURNACE narrative (Daniel 3:19-27 — fire cannot harm Shadrach + Meshach + Abednego) + the JONAH-IN-THE-FISH preservation (Jonah 1:17 + 2:10) + Christian-martyr-acts hagiographic tradition of incorruptible relics (Polycarp's body found unburned in the flames; Eulalia's incorruptible body in Prudentius Peristephanon 3). The Meqabyan version compresses the four-fold elemental-failure (fire/water/land-beast/sky-bird) into one chapter as a complete-cosmos resistance.

candidates.draft_body:
Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

'They did so; but the beasts and the carrion-birds did not touch their corpses. CARRION-BIRDS AND BIRDS OF THE AIR COVERED THEM WITH THEIR WINGS, that they might be a covering for the holy ones' — divine-protection-by-wings continuation of the corpses-resist-destruction motif. The bird-protection motif extends Psalm 91:4 ('he shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust') from the living to the martyred-dead. Tewahedo iconography of the saint-protected-by-divine-bird-wings (found across Aksumite manuscript-illumination) is rooted in this verse-tradition. The chapter closes (4:6ff.) with angels joining the bird-protection and the corpses being preserved for forty days before being taken to Paradise — completing the martyr-cult preservation cycle that the Tewahedo Sǝnkǝsar (Synaxarium) recapitulates for every commemorated saint.
